content: The United Nations International Drug Control Programme (UNDCP) and the United Nations Centre for International Crime Prevention (CICP) are integral components of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), which was previously known as the United Nations Office for Drug Control & Crime Prevention (ODCCP). The UNDCP collaborates extensively with both governmental and non-governmental organizations, as well as with private sector entities. Currently, it is formulating strategies to enhance its engagement with the private sector in a more focused and systematic manner. The UNDCP employs a team of experts who assist countries in becoming parties to the United Nations drug control conventions and in implementing these conventions effectively. Additionally, the UNDCP provides laboratory services, develops training materials, and offers referrals to appropriate medical advice for those in need. In central, eastern, and southeastern Europe, the UNDCP has concentrated its efforts on fostering cross-border cooperation by harmonizing national drug control capacities. A significant aspect of its work in this region has been the creation of a coordination mechanism to streamline international drug control assistance for eastern Europe, the Baltic States, and the Commonwealth of Independent States. An external evaluation has underscored the necessity of such coordination mechanisms due to the complexity of the recipient countries' needs and the involvement of multiple donors in the region. This mechanism has been instrumental in aligning strategies among donor countries and international organizations in the realm of drug control. The UNDCP coordination mechanism has increasingly been utilized to develop joint strategies between the UNDCP and donors, as well as to design and implement technical cooperation projects and programs. Efforts to further refine and expand this mechanism were ongoing during the years 2000-2001. In the domain of demand reduction, the UNDCP successfully completed a multiphase regional program aimed at training professionals in the treatment of drug abuse. This initiative resulted in the establishment of a core group of over 600 trained professionals and the development of sustainable national training programs. The UNDCP has also collaborated with the Pompidou Group of the Council of Europe to extend its city network to include states in eastern Europe. Furthermore, it has partnered with the International Labour Organization (ILO) to implement a workplace prevention program funded by the UNDCP and has worked with the Associazione Casa Famiglia Rosetta to train professionals in drug abuse treatment.
